title: Skribly
kind: Developer tools for AI coding agents
tagline: From a task to an approved commit
summary: Skribly is a private project I build with four friends. It is a family of developer tools for people who write software with AI coding agents, and it is non-commercial: nothing is sold, it has no clients and offers no services. Skribly Agent is a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that runs AI coding agents side by side and shows which one is working, which waits for a decision and which has finished; it is in development and its installers are not public yet. agent-skills gives seven coding agents 38 portable skills for tests, reviews, audits and clean commits that adapt to each project through a project profile. Skribly Tracker is the issue tracker of the family, built on Node.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL, with Kanban boards and a REST API of 53 operations checked by contract tests; it is in development and not deployed. Skribly Core holds the shared contracts and the server kit the apps are built on, Skribly UI is the design system, built to WCAG 2.2 AA as a target and shown at ui.skribly.pl, and Skribly Docs explains all of it at docs.skribly.pl in English and Polish. Being added, and not public yet: one sign-in for the apps (Skribly ID), one address for their APIs (Skribly API), a local console of the repositories (Skribly Hub), a few small sites and the templates new apps and sites start from. Co-created with Piotr Smoła, Michał Pilecki, Konrad Pluta and Mateusz Olko; the repositories stay private while we build.
metaDescription: Skribly is a private, non-commercial project of five developers: developer tools for planning work and building software with AI coding agents.

Agents you can watch while they work

title: CV
tagline: The page is the source, the PDF is the export
summary: CV is my curriculum vitae as a website, in Polish and English. The page is the original; the PDFs in this repository are printed from it. One layout means the two versions cannot drift apart, and the print stylesheet is tuned so the browser's own Save as PDF produces exactly the single A4 sheet that is checked in.
shows: The print output is the deliverable

title: ZbudujKompa
kind: Bilingual reference website for PC builders
tagline: Build your PC without guessing
summary: ZbudujKompa is a reference site for anyone assembling a computer, published in Polish and English. It covers CPU platforms and sockets, cooling classes, a catalogue of real components, complete reference builds and step-by-step assembly guides — including installing Windows and Linux, which most build guides skip entirely. Each recommendation ships with the reasoning behind it rather than just the verdict.

title: MP Industries
tagline: Four businesses, one website
summary: MP Industries is a company website for a business that runs in four directions at once: CNC machinery, LPG installations, dog breeding and natural honey. Rather than flattening those into one generic page, each branch gets the model it actually needs — machines have categories and specifications, dogs have breeds and litters with breeding documents, honey has products and categories.

title: CVForge
kind: CV builder that runs in the browser
tagline: The preview is the print
summary: CVForge turns a form into a finished CV. Fill in your details, choose one of six templates, and print an A4 sheet that looks exactly like the preview. A separate tab reviews the document the way an applicant tracking system would, and tells you what it found.
shows: The preview is the printed sheet
Open the finished CV in its own tab
Import an existing CV from a PDF
An ATS check that explains itself
Six templates, one set of content

title: ReelCut
kind: Video editor that runs in the browser
tagline: The footage never leaves the tab
summary: ReelCut is a video editor that runs inside a browser tab. Load a clip from disk, split it on the timeline, switch off the parts you do not want, crop it to the shape the platform wants, correct picture and sound, and render a finished file you can download straight away.
shows: A render that actually produces a file

title: NeoBank
tagline: Fullstack Retail Banking Platform
summary: NeoBank is a working retail banking system built from scratch with Nuxt 4, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL — not a UI mock-up. Balances are derived from an immutable double-entry ledger, and money can only move through transactions that are guaranteed to balance. Customers hold multi-currency accounts with checksum-correct IBANs, send internal and external transfers, schedule standing orders and export statements; administrators manage users and review an append-only audit trail.

title: BodyKit
kind: Front-end web shop with static export
tagline: A front-end shop for car body kits and styling parts
summary: BodyKit Shop is a complete front-end store selling body modification parts: front splitters, spoilers, diffusers, wheels and carbon fibre components. There is no backend — the whole thing compiles to static HTML that can be hosted on GitHub Pages, any CDN, or behind nginx in a container.

title: EzPace
tagline: A plan counted back from the race date, not bolted onto it
summary: EzPace is a product site for a running coach. Three plans, a calculator that actually computes, the coaching process and real-looking results. The premise is that a training plan is derived from the race date rather than appended to it, and every section on the page argues that point.
shows: A pace calculator that is not a mock-up
Splits that include the leftover distance

title: EzScout
tagline: A report that says whether he is worth buying
summary: EzScout is a product site for a football scouting service: packages, process, results and an enquiry form. The premise is deliberately narrow — data collected by hand, minute by minute, and conclusions written by the person who did the watching. Every section on the page exists to support that one claim.
shows: A sample report card in the hero
Form that admits what it is

title: Airline Passenger Satisfaction
tagline: Multiclass flight-class prediction with a PyTorch MLP built from scratch
summary: A multiclass project that predicts the flight class (Business, Eco or Eco Plus) on the Airline Passenger Satisfaction dataset from Kaggle. The main model is a multilayer perceptron built from scratch in PyTorch, with a scikit-learn Random Forest as the reference. Preprocessing is fitted on the training split alone, hyperparameters come from an 18-configuration grid search on a dedicated validation split, and the test split is touched exactly once at the end.

title: Cyber Security Attacks Classifier
tagline: End-to-end multiclass classification of network attacks
summary: A machine learning project that classifies network security events into three attack types — DDoS, Malware and Intrusion — using the Cyber Security Attacks dataset from Kaggle. The primary model is a Random Forest; Gradient Boosting and k-NN are trained alongside it for comparison. A Streamlit dashboard walks through exploratory analysis, preprocessing, model design, comparison and evaluation.

title: Wine Quality Classification
tagline: Multiclass wine quality classification with leakage-free scikit-learn pipelines
summary: An end-to-end machine learning study on the Wine Quality dataset. Nine classifier variants — Decision Tree, k-NN and Random Forest, three hyperparameter settings each — are evaluated with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, alongside a VotingClassifier ensemble that aggregates all nine by majority vote.

title: BitRecruit
tagline: IT Career Platform
summary: BitRecruit is a modern IT job board platform built with Next.js 13, React 18, Mantine UI and Tailwind CSS. It ships with built-in mock data — 48 realistic job offers generated at build time — so the whole application runs client-side with no server required.

title: CinemaReserve
tagline: Full-Stack Cinema Seat Reservation Platform
summary: CinemaReserve is a full-stack cinema booking application inspired by real-world systems such as Multikino and Helios. Visitors browse the "Now Showing" catalogue, pick a screening, choose seats on an interactive colour-coded seat map, and manage their own reservations. Administrators get a Berry-inspired panel covering movies, screenings, halls, users, reservations and site content.

title: DevPulse
kind: Developer blog as a React single-page app
tagline: Modern Developer Tech Blog with React & TypeScript
summary: DevPulse is a modern developer tech blog built as a single-page React application with TypeScript, Ant Design and Styled Components. It presents practical engineering articles across categories such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, DevOps, System Design, AI & ML, Web Performance and Career.

title: MovieVault
tagline: Full-Stack Movie Review Platform
summary: MovieVault is a full-stack movie review platform inspired by IMDb and Filmweb. Users can browse a catalogue of movies, write and rate reviews, curate a personal watchlist, and explore detailed platform statistics. Critic reviews are weighted differently from regular user reviews, giving the rating system an editorial dimension.

title: SmartRecommender
tagline: Full-Stack Product Recommendation Platform
summary: SmartRecommender is a full-stack e-commerce platform that delivers personalized product recommendations by combining collaborative filtering, content analysis, association mining, fuzzy logic, sentiment analysis and probabilistic modelling. Every recommendation method is implemented from the ground up on top of NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn rather than pulled in from a ready-made recommender library, which makes the repository as much a study of the algorithms as it is a shop.

title: HirudoZdrowie
tagline: A clinic site that answers before it sells
summary: HirudoZdrowie is the website of a Polish hirudotherapy clinic — treatment with medicinal leeches. Most of it is explanation rather than promotion: what the therapy is, what it is indicated for, what it is contraindicated for, how to prepare, and what the results look like. The contact page and the FAQ are there for the questions the pages do not already answer.

title: WorkStation
tagline: Interactive Gaming & Work Setup Showcase with Vue 3 + TypeScript
summary: WorkStation is an interactive portfolio for visualizing a complete gaming and productivity workspace. Built with Vue 3, TypeScript and Vite, it breaks a real setup down into six hardware categories — PC, laptop, monitors, peripherals, audio and workspace — each with its own category page, per-component detail page, photo gallery and full technical specifications.

title: ANFIS vs Classical Machine Learning
tagline: A model that can be read out loud
summary: ANFIS vs Classical ML puts an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System next to SVM and Random Forest on two real datasets — wine quality (classification) and concrete compressive strength (regression) — and measures them on identical splits with a single seed.
shows: Both task types on the same footing

title: IT Help Desk
tagline: Modern IT Help Desk Ticketing System
summary: IT Help Desk System manages technical support requests inside an organisation: an ASP.NET Core 9.0 REST API behind a Vue 3 + TypeScript single-page application, covering the ticket lifecycle, role-based access, search and filtering.

title: TaskApp
tagline: Four roles, four applications
summary: TaskApp manages projects, teams and tasks for an IT company. An administrator, a manager, a team leader and an employee each sign into the same application and get a different interface: separate FXML trees, separate controllers, separate dashboards. A role does not simply hide buttons — it loads a different view.
shows: Projects, teams and members as real relations

title: DataFusion
kind: Python desktop application for data preparation
tagline: A CSV workbench that runs on the desktop
summary: DataFusion is a desktop application for the part of data science that comes before the model: opening a file, finding out what is wrong with it, and fixing it. Load a CSV or one of the two bundled UCI datasets, read the statistics, fill or drop the missing values, encode the categorical columns, scale the numeric ones, and draw the chart that shows whether any of it worked.
shows: Both correlation matrices, side by side
Missing values handled by strategy, not by hand

title: FrameVision
tagline: One page, five sections, no framework
summary: FrameVision is a single-page site for a photography studio: opening header, about, services, team and contact. Sections reveal as they enter the viewport, the navigation gains a background once you scroll past the header, a scroll-to-top button appears after 450 pixels, and a booking modal collects a name and a phone number with its own validation.
shows: A navigation that reacts to position
A burger menu that closes itself
A scroll-to-top button that stays out of the way

title: Rent App
tagline: Filters that show their work
summary: Rent App is the search page of a property developer's site: a list of flats with a filter panel above it. Floor, area and price are range sliders; project, finishing standard and completion deadline are dropdowns. Whatever is active appears as a labelled chip with its own clear button, so the list never quietly hides results behind a filter you forgot you set.
shows: Active filters are visible and individually clearable
Three range sliders, not six number fields
An icon set as files, not a font

title: Kebab
tagline: The cart is in one place
summary: Kebab is an ordering page for a kebab restaurant: the menu, a sidebar cart and a checkout preview. The cart lives in a React context with a reducer, because three separate parts of the tree need it at once — the add buttons on each product, the counter in the navbar and the panel that lists what you picked. Passing it down as props would have meant threading state through every layer between them.
shows: A sidebar, not a separate page

title: Shop
tagline: The same shop, without a backend
summary: Shop — Vue + Firestore is the serverless twin of a classic Laravel storefront. The catalogue, baskets, purchases and checkout details live in Firestore collections; the Vue 3 app reads and writes them directly, and Firebase Authentication decides who may write what. There is no API layer in between, because the security rules are the API layer.
shows: The dataset ships with the code

title: Employee Directory
tagline: 300 000 employees, one query at a time
summary: Employee Directory puts a readable interface on the MySQL Employees sample database — the one with six tables, three hundred thousand people and forty years of salary history. It lists them with pagination, narrows the list by department, gender, salary range and employment status, and opens a single person's record with their titles, departments and pay over time.

title: Layout Simple
kind: Vue landing page built from components
tagline: Content lives in files, not in templates
summary: Layout Simple is a corporate landing page rebuilt out of nine independent sections: navbar, slider, services, industries, products, news, partner logos, sidebar and footer. Each one is a component with two companions — a data module under src/data and a stylesheet under src/styles — so changing the wording or the figures never means opening a template.
shows: A slider, a logo wall and a news strip
A sidebar that folds on mobile

title: Shop App
tagline: A basket that survives the browser
summary: Shop App is a full-stack shop. Vue 3 renders the storefront — catalogue, categories, brands, product pages, basket and checkout — and Laravel 11 serves it over a JSON API secured with Sanctum. The basket is a table in the database, tied to the signed-in user, so it is still there on the next device and the next day.
shows: The basket is a table, not browser state
Browse by category or by brand

title: Weather App
kind: Full-stack Laravel and React weather app
tagline: Weather that remembers
summary: Weather App shows the current weather for Polish cities and keeps every reading it fetches. A logged-in user builds their own list of cities; the backend asks OpenWeatherMap for the conditions, writes the answer into the database and serves the history back, so each city has a chart of where the temperature has actually been — not just where it is right now.
shows: Search any city in the world
A five-day forecast beside the current reading

title: WiFiDirect File Transfer
tagline: Two phones, no network
summary: WiFiDirect File Transfer moves files straight between two Android devices. Wi-Fi Direct negotiates the link, one device becomes the sender and the other the receiver, and the bytes go over a socket between them. Nothing is uploaded, nothing passes through a server, and the two phones do not need to be on the same network — or on any network at all.
shows: Sender and receiver are separate screens

title: dawidolko.pl
tagline: Multi-page personal website built from scratch
summary: dawidolko.pl is my personal website and the central hub of my work. It is a static, multi-page site written without a frontend framework: every page is semantic HTML, styles are authored in modular SASS, and interactivity is plain ES modules bundled with webpack. The site collects my projects, academic path, hobbies and a photo blog in one place.

title: Language Courses
tagline: Enrolment, not just a catalogue
summary: Language Courses is a course enrolment platform. Visitors browse the catalogue, open a course to see its lessons and teacher, and add it to a basket with the date they want. Checking out turns the basket into enrolments — real rows against the user, each with a lesson date and a status — rather than an order that somebody has to type into a system afterwards.
shows: A date chosen at the point of buying
An admin area that covers the whole model

title: TechByte
tagline: A shop that runs on Oracle
summary: TechByte is a computer store: laptops, desktops, components and accessories, with a basket, favourites, opinions, complaints and a newsletter. What makes it different from a standard Laravel shop is the database — it runs against Oracle 19c through yajra/laravel-oci8, and a good part of the logic sits in PL/SQL procedures and functions rather than in controllers.
shows: Logic in PL/SQL where it belongs
Favourites and a basket per account
Opinions and complaints as first-class records

title: RentalVOD
tagline: Rules the admin can rewrite
summary: RentalVOD rents films. A visitor browses the catalogue, a signed-in user fills a basket, checks out and gets a loan with a return date; a premium upgrade unlocks the extended version of a title. Around that sit loyalty points, referral codes, friendships, opinions and recommendations between users.

title: WidgetMart
tagline: Nine pages, one browser
summary: WidgetMart is a full shop front built without a framework or a backend: home, products, product detail, gallery, cart, services, about, FAQ, contact and privacy. The cart persists between visits, a live weather panel pulls from OpenWeatherMap, a note manager keeps its own list, the theme switch remembers your choice and the cookie banner remembers that you dismissed it.
shows: Live weather with a search history
A note manager as a real class
A cookie banner that stays dismissed

title: ATM Simulator
tagline: A cash machine with a real ledger
summary: ATM Simulator reproduces the flow of a cash machine: insert a card, enter a PIN, check the balance, withdraw, deposit, pay a bill, review the transaction history. The state lives in MySQL — cards, balances and history are three tables — so closing the application and reopening it finds the account exactly where it was left.
shows: State in the database, not in the process
A PIN gate with card selection
Four operations, each its own window
History as a table, backed by a model

title: Curiosities Magazine
tagline: Sixteen pages, no JavaScript
summary: Curiosities Magazine is a website template for a magazine that also sells: home, articles, three product pages with their own checkout screens, gallery, services, about, FAQ, contact and privacy — sixteen pages in all. Every layout, every hover state and every breakpoint is CSS — no scripted behaviour anywhere, which was the constraint it was built under.

title: FitnessGym
kind: React marketing site with a shop
tagline: A gym site with a shop attached
summary: FitnessGym is a marketing site for a gym that happens to sell things. Seven pages — home, about, shop, cart, blog, FAQ and contact — with scroll-triggered sections, an animated counter, a testimonial slider and a map. The shop keeps its cart in localStorage, so closing the tab does not empty it.
shows: A cart that survives a refresh
Forms that validate before they submit

title: F1 Zone
tagline: A poster shop without a framework
summary: F1 Zone sells Formula 1 posters: tracks, cars and drivers. The catalogue lives in a JavaScript data file, a modal opens any poster full size, and the cart keeps its contents in localStorage, so closing the tab does not empty it.
shows: A cart that survives the tab
A product modal built by hand

title: Windows Desktop Portfolio
kind: Portfolio shaped like a Windows desktop
tagline: A portfolio that boots
summary: Instead of a page with sections, this portfolio opens as a desktop. Windows drag, resize and stack, the start menu works, the wallpaper changes, and each "application" is a part of the CV — projects, contact, notes.
shows: A contact form without a backend
credit: Based on Portfolio_OS_Theme by Srinibas Biswal

title: Ubuntu Desktop Portfolio
kind: Portfolio shaped like an Ubuntu desktop
tagline: GNOME, rebuilt as a static site
summary: A portfolio shaped like Ubuntu 20.04: the dock down the left, draggable windows, the dark-orange palette and the GNOME behaviours that go with them.
shows: A GNOME dock and window behaviour
A contact form without a backend
credit: Based on vivek9patel.github.io by Vivek Patel

title: Deepin Desktop Portfolio
kind: Portfolio shaped like a Deepin desktop
tagline: A desktop with a blog inside it
summary: A portfolio and blog wearing the Deepin Linux desktop. Windows open, move, resize and layer as they do on the real system, and the applications are not decorative: a toy terminal, a music player, a recursive file system and a blog whose articles are markdown files rendered in a window.
shows: A blog that lives in a window

title: macOS Desktop Portfolio
kind: Portfolio shaped like a macOS desktop
tagline: The dock, the launchpad and the animations
summary: A macOS desktop in the browser: the dock with its magnification, launchpad, draggable windows, and an appearance that follows the system light/dark preference.
credit: Based on playground-macos by Xiaohan Zou

title: Website Templates
tagline: 170 templates, all of them openable
summary: Website Templates is a collection of 170 free, editable HTML templates — portfolios, business sites, blogs, shops, agencies, restaurants, photography and more. Every one of them is checked in whole, and every one has a working preview: the whole repository is published through GitHub Pages, so a template can be opened and judged before it is downloaded.

title: GitHub Achievements
tagline: Every badge, with the numbers behind it
summary: GitHub Achievements documents the badges that appear on a GitHub profile: what each one is, how it is earned, and exactly how many actions each tier takes. Where GitHub states a requirement, it is here; where it does not, the entry says so rather than guessing.

title: Portfolio
tagline: Personal portfolio website of Dawid Olko
summary: Portfolio is a personal website built as a single-page React application. It has a dark theme, a card grid of projects, a photo blog with a lightbox viewer, a built-in PDF viewer for the resume and an about page with a GitHub activity calendar.

title: WordPress Cinema
tagline: A cinema in two containers
summary: WordPress Cinema is a cinema website built on WordPress and run in Docker. docker compose up starts WordPress on port 8080 and MySQL 8 beside it; wp-content is mounted from the repository, so the custom theme, the plugins and the uploads are version-controlled while the WordPress core stays where it belongs — inside the image.
shows: One command from nothing to a running site
wp-content in git, core in the image
